title: Guitarist Joseph Phillip and Lonnie Johnson 'Rooster'
summary: Joseph Phillip, a fine fingerstyle guitarist now in Florida, and Lonnie Johnson, who played guitar and trumpet with Miller around Bayou Lafourche.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: What about guitar players? Did they have any guitar players out there?
In church? Oh yeah, they had them and a boy named Joseph Phillip. Boy, he could pick a guitar. My God. I never heard nobody play a guitar like him.
I wonder what ever happened to him.
He's right over here in, wait now I'll call it, Semio, Florida. Not Semio, no. Boy that place has got a funny name. Kasemi. Kasemi. Kasemi, Florida. That's a, we call it a cattle town.
He'd be easy to find over there you think?
Yeah, I'll write him. He played bass now and guitar.
Do you remember if he used a pick or did he use finger style?
Pick with his hands? With his fingers. Yeah, with his fingers and then he could rap too.
Yeah, yeah. Oh he was a guitar man.
Oh yeah, well he'd be worth looking up.
And I'll tell you another fella I worked with a long time. Of course we all call him Rooster. But his name is Lonnie Johnson. You heard of him.

Well me and him play together with guitar and trumpet up and down Bollyfoot long time ago. It's guitar and trumpet. Lonnie Johnson. But we all call him Rooster at home. Well where is he from? He's from uh somewhere out from Memphis. Not on, not in Memphis.
Out from Memphis. A little small place. I believe it's Tennessee City or something like that. Mm-hmm.
Yeah. And he uh used to hang around the Bayou Lafourche area though. Yeah. That's right.
